title: Condensed realization preserves the specified compact-support compositor
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y,Z$, and smooth $k$-morphisms $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$; put $h=g\circ f$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. On each small pro-etale site set $A_{n,T}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_T$, $R_T=\varprojlim_n A_{n,T}$, and let $\mathcal I_T$ be the completed integral constructible category with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z_\ell$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Use the ordinary derived category of strict semilinear coefficient systems with componentwise exactness, the actual reduction/total-limit adjunction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T=R\varprojlim\operatorname{Res}$, and its counit $e_T:\mathcal R_T\mathcal L_T\to1$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

For $v=f,g,h$, let $\mathcal F_v$ be the actual strict-system proper/open compact-support functor for the chosen Nagata compactification $c_v=(i_v,p_v)$, namely $Rp_{v,*,\bullet}i_{v,!,\bullet}$, and let $P_v:\mathcal I_{\operatorname{source}(v)}\to\mathcal I_{\operatorname{target}(v)}$ be its specified total-limit compact-support reconstruction with actual comparison $\beta_v:\mathcal R P_v\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_v\mathcal R$ [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. Write $\delta_v:P_v\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L\mathcal F_v\mathcal R$ for $\mathcal L(\beta_v)$ after the reduction/limit unit. For the assertions below, restrict to $K\in\mathcal I_X$ whose normalized reductions have cohomology and Tor amplitude in common finite intervals independent of $n$: tensor with any degree-zero $A_{n,X}$-module has cohomology in the chosen Tor interval. The tower functors are restricted to the uniform constructible finite-Tor subcategories and their normalized parts. On these subcategories use the proper/open compositor $\alpha_\bullet:\mathcal F_g\mathcal F_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_h$ of [lem-sp-tower-adjoint-compositor-realization], with the finite coefficient composition identities: the $b$ identity is the composition equation of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] on bounded constructible etale origins [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], and the $c$ identity is its transpose by [lem-sp-finite-adjoint-compositor-transposes]. Its normalization uses proper direct-image composition, composition of open extensions, the proper/open interchange, and the canonical compactification comparisons. For such a $K$, define $\alpha_R(K):P_gP_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_hK$ by the following actual composite, with associators understood:
$$P_gP_fK\xrightarrow{\delta_g(P_fK)}\mathcal L_Z\mathcal F_g\mathcal R_YP_fK\xrightarrow{\mathcal L_Z\mathcal F_g\mathcal R_Y(\delta_f(K))}\mathcal L_Z\mathcal F_g\mathcal R_Y\mathcal L_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_XK\xrightarrow{\mathcal L_Z\mathcal F_g(e_{Y,\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_XK})}\mathcal L_Z\mathcal F_g\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_XK\xrightarrow{\mathcal L_Z(\alpha_\bullet)}\mathcal L_Z\mathcal F_h\mathcal R_XK\xrightarrow{\delta_h(K)^{-1}}P_hK.$$

Let $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $E_T^c=p_T^*C(-,E)$, and $B_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous functions on a profinite set $S$ with values in one finite intermediate extension of $E$ in $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Use the specified realization $J_T:\mathcal I_T[1/\ell]\simeq\mathcal C_E^c(T)$ and $U_T(M)=B_T\otimes^L_{E_T^c}J_T(M[1/\ell])$ [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. Let $F_v=Rv_{!,\Omega}$ be the bounded constructible condensed-module compact-support functor for $c_v$, and let $a_v:U_{\operatorname{target}(v)}P_v\xrightarrow{\sim}F_vU_{\operatorname{source}(v)}$ be exactly the composite of the rational compact-support comparison and its $E\to\Omega$ projection comparison specified in [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. Let $\alpha_\Omega:F_gF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_h$ be the proper/open normalized condensed compositor: the inverse of $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleLowerShriekComp\_padicAlgCl}(\ell,f,g)$, with its specified chosen-compactification refinement, open-extension compositor, proper direct-image compositor and proper/open exchange, not an arbitrary isomorphism between these functors [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek]. Then for every such $K$ the following equality holds in $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(Z)$:
$$a_h(K)\circ U_Z(\alpha_R(K))=\alpha_\Omega(U_XK)\circ F_g(a_f(K))\circ a_g(P_fK).$$
The equality is natural in $K$ and compatible with replacing the three chosen compactifications by compatible compactification towers and common refinements. Equivalently the same square holds for any such compactifications after transporting $\alpha_\Omega$ by their canonical comparisons with the chosen ones. In particular, when $g$ is open, its compactification can be $(g,\mathrm{id}_Z)$, with $F_g$ identified with exact extension by zero through the specified trivial-compactification comparison. The definition of $\alpha_R$ uses the actual strict-system compositor and the actual total-limit units and counits before rationalization; finite evaluations are not assumed faithful on derived morphisms. No purity orientation or choice of a trace is part of this assertion.

proof.text: For a chosen compactification $c_v=(i_v,p_v)$ write $Q_v=Rp_{v,*,R}i_{v,!,R}$ for the ordinary completed-ring proper/open word, and write $\alpha_Q:Q_gQ_f\to Q_h$ for its normalized proper/open word. All ambient schemes in a chosen compatible tower are finite type over $k$; they are Noetherian and finite dimensional, and $\ell$ is invertible. Thus $Q_v$ takes integral constructible complete objects to such objects. The input reductions have the additional uniform finite-Tor bounds required in the item; the system functors preserve these bounds and normalized systems by the cited tower theorem. In particular every occurrence of $P_gP_f$, $Q_gQ_f$ and their reductions below has the stated domain. We use no integral-equivalence assertion restricted to $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$: all operations here are on the actual small sites over the given $k$.

proof.text: Pass first from completed coefficient sheaves to their constant diagrams on the vertical sequence sites. The diagonal $\Delta$ is exact and is right adjoint to evaluation at index $1$: a map of inverse systems $N\to\Delta M$ is uniquely the map $N_1\to M$ followed at index $n$ by $N_n\to N_1$. Evaluation is exact, so $\Delta$ preserves K-injectives by the cited theorem. On a K-injective representative the direct-image comparison is therefore the literal identity $p_{*,\bullet}\Delta I=\Delta p_*I$. Diagonal inverse image and open extension are the same degreewise operations. Their units, counits, pullback and open compositors are the diagonal ordinary maps; the direct-image compositor is their adjunction conjugate. Mate pasting then identifies the diagonal of the completed proper/open mate with its constant-diagram mate: its open comparison is identity on the open, and its clopen projector is $(1,0)$ on the two components before and after diagonal. These identities are constructed before localization, then on K-injective models, rather than inferred from equal evaluated arrows.

proof.text:
On these diagram sites apply coefficient change $\Delta R_T\to A_{\bullet,T}$, with its actual quotient homomorphisms. The completed structural maps commute with these quotients by the coefficient inverse-image theorem. Its proper counit transpose followed by its open comparison gives a whole-system natural map
$$b_v:\mathcal R Q_v\longrightarrow\mathcal F_v\mathcal R.$$
The proper factor is the specified diagram-site projection map of the direct-image/limit theorem; it is invertible since $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ is perfect over $\mathbf Z_\ell$ (the two-term resolution by multiplication by $\ell^n$), and the input is complete. The open factor is invertible by open tensor normalization. Proper direct-image composition is conjugate to pullback composition, so mate pasting carries its coefficient square to the square for the composite. Open composition has the same coefficient square since both open adjuncts are the identity. The new single-square theorem supplies the coefficient square for the proper/open factor, also for noncartesian refinement factors; the ringed refinement coefficient theorem gives it for refinement transformations. The word $\alpha_Q$ inverts completed refinement comparisons, so each single completed proper/open or refinement factor $\Gamma$ of the word is first shown invertible on the inputs that occur. These inputs are $K$ and $i_{!,R}K$, which lie in the completed constructible category with compatible bounded-below etale-origin witnesses by the integral compact-support restriction theorem (for $i_!$ use the identity as proper factor). The coefficient square reads $b\,\mathcal R(\Gamma)=\Gamma_\bullet\,b$ with both $b$ invertible. By the semilinear mate-pasting theorem, termwise restriction to constant $\mathbf Z_\ell$-towers identifies $\Gamma_\bullet$ with the constant-tower mate, which is invertible on such witnessed inputs by the strict-tower proper/open calculus; evaluations and restriction of scalars jointly detect isomorphisms by the semilinear section theorem. Hence $\mathcal R(\Gamma)$ is invertible, and naturality of the unit with the invertible completion units at its complete source and target makes $\Gamma$ invertible. Thus $\alpha_Q$ is defined. Paste these individual squares (inverse squares for inverted factors), including their outside functors, in the defining compactification word. It gives, as an equality of actual semilinear-system maps,
$$b_h\mathcal R(\alpha_Q)=\alpha_\bullet\circ\mathcal F_g(b_f)\circ b_g(Q_f). \tag{1}$$
The tower theorem identifies the target word here with its specified $\alpha_\bullet$, not with an isomorphism chosen from its finite evaluations. Equation (1) and the invertible $b$ show that $\mathcal R(\alpha_Q)$ is invertible. Applying $\mathcal L$ and the natural invertible completion units at $Q_gQ_fK,Q_hK$ proves invertibility of $\alpha_Q$; no faithfulness of finite evaluations is needed.

proof.text: The refinementIso_exists auxiliary is now proved directly on the ordinary derived semilinear system category. For the actual completed coefficient object M of K, finiteTorConstructibleIntegral gives intrinsic constructibility of every finite scalar reduction and one common finite cohomological interval [a,b]. Restriction to constant scalars gives finite-model constructibility. The positive_stratification helper gives a positive global partition, including the empty scheme. The finite-model locality and geometric-stalk lemmas identify its strata with fixed-module lisse strata with finite stalks, hence fixed-module constructibility. The proved scalar_origin helper packages bounded etale descent as a ScalarEtaleOrigin for each finite reduction. The exact derived composition comparison identifies E_n followed by constant-diagram evaluation at any q with coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation at n; composing with reductionEvaluation transports those witnesses to E_n(R(M)). Apply StrictTower.gamma_isIso to this constant quotient-ring diagram. The equation gamma_evaluation, together with invertibility of evalR and evalJ, makes E_n of the actual semilinear gamma invertible. Evaluation at zero and the same exact composition comparison recover ordinary system evaluation. The detects clause of the semilinear derived section calculus proves that gamma itself is invertible. In the refinement square use c.i, identity_X, r.hom, d.i. systemRefinement is the paste of this gamma with the identity-proper unitor, a whiskering by d.g, the functor associator, and the proper compositor; all are invertible. Package asIso with its hom equality to obtain RefinementIso. This argument is for arbitrary CoefficientData A and needs no field-of-definition condition, no equality detection by evaluations, and no new assumed statement.

proof.text:
Let $u,e$ denote the actual reduction/limit unit and counit. Define the comparison with reconstruction by
$$q_v=\delta_v^{-1}\circ\mathcal L(b_v)\circ u_{Q_v}:Q_v\longrightarrow P_v.$$
Completeness makes $u_{Q_v}$ invertible; hence $q_v$ is invertible. Since $\delta_v=\mathcal L(\beta_v)u_{P_v}$ is the adjunct of $\beta_v$, its counit equation is $e\mathcal R(\delta_v)=\beta_v$. Naturality of $e$ and the triangle identity now give
$$\beta_v\mathcal R(q_v)=b_v. \tag{2}$$
This uses the whole-system comparisons. In the comparison $a_{v,E}$ specified in the item, the first arrow is the inverse of precisely this projection-normalized $q_v$, followed by rational realization; the remaining arrows are the proper scalar counit transpose and the open scalar comparison. Indeed its reduction/limit portion is $\mathcal L(b_v)u_{Q_v}$, and its proper/open portion is exactly the original coefficient projection. The limit-unit and coefficient-transpose descriptions fix these arrows, not only their endpoints. Write this normalization as
$$a_{v,E}J(q_v)=z_{v,E}, \tag{3}$$
where $z_{v,E}:J(Q_v[1/\ell])\to F_{v,E}J$ is that ordered proper/open scalar map. The Lean proof of delta_isIso first proves the generic adjunction identity u_V L(R(v) e_W)=v for v:V→L(W), using unit naturality and the right triangle. By the definition of beta=R(limitPresentation)e, delta is consequently exactly limitPresentation on each K, hence is invertible.

proof.text:
Equation (1) identifies the reconstructed compositor without any test of finite evaluations. Put
$$q_{g,f}=P_g(q_f)\circ q_g(Q_f):Q_gQ_f\longrightarrow P_gP_f.$$
Substitute $q_v=\delta_v^{-1}\mathcal L(b_v)u_{Q_v}$ and the displayed definition of $\alpha_R$ into $\alpha_Rq_{g,f}$. Move $q_f$ through $\delta_g$ by naturality. The adjacent reduction/limit unit and counit cancel by $e\mathcal R(\delta_f)=\beta_f$ and (2). What remains is
$$\alpha_Rq_{g,f}=\delta_h^{-1}\mathcal L\bigl(\alpha_\bullet\mathcal F_g(b_f)b_g(Q_f)\bigr)u_{Q_gQ_f}.$$
Replace the parenthesis by $b_h\mathcal R(\alpha_Q)$ using (1), and use naturality of $u$. This is exactly
$$\alpha_Rq_{g,f}=q_h\alpha_Q. \tag{4}$$
All operations in this calculation are functors or natural transformations of the ordinary derived system categories. In particular $\alpha_R$ is invertible because (4), $q$ and the normalized proper/open word are invertible on these inputs.

proof.text:
Now perform scalar change $R_T\to E_T^c$ on the ordinary ringed sites. The realization theorem identifies $J$ with this actual derived coefficient extension and identifies its proper direct-image comparisons with the counit mates; the open comparison is the open-unit-normalized one. Apply the new single-square coefficient theorem to each proper/open factor. For the proper and open composition factors use adjunction-compatible direct-image composition and mate pasting, exactly as in Step 3. The result is
$$z_{h,E}J(\alpha_Q)=\alpha_E\circ F_{g,E}(z_{f,E})\circ z_{g,E}(Q_f). \tag{5}$$
Here $\alpha_E$ is the inverse of the actual condensed chosen-compactification composition construction: its factors are the chosen compactification comparison, proper compositor, open compositor and normalized proper/open interchange. This identifies the specified map by its constituent maps and their adjunction normalizations. Raw rationalization preserves the equality: it is a functor, and $J$ and all comparisons are precisely those of its localization, so neither a choice of a lattice morphism nor a faithfulness assertion after scalar restriction is used.

proof.text:
Let $T_T=B_T\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ and let $\rho_v:TF_{v,E}\to F_vT$ be the original proper coefficient transpose followed by open coefficient comparison. The compact-support realization theorem says these maps are invertible for the finite-extension-valued coefficient ring $B_T$ in the item. Apply the ordinary-site case of the new single-square theorem directly to $E_T^c\to B_T$, not to a discrete algebraic-closure sheaf. Pasting with proper/open compositors as in Step 6 gives
$$\rho_hT(\alpha_E)=\alpha_\Omega\circ F_g(\rho_f)\circ\rho_g(F_{f,E}). \tag{6}$$
The condensed-to-sectionwise module equivalence preserves the underlying sections identically. Its geometric adjunctions are thereby the same section adjunctions: transposition is the ordinary restriction/section Hom formula. Deriving on corresponding K-injective resolutions gives the same units, counits and hence these original internal-module maps. This argument needs no commutation of an unbounded direct image with a filtered colimit: existence and invertibility of $\rho$ are supplied by the realization theorem, and the equality is a coefficient-mate identity for an arbitrary ring-sheaf map. By the item $a_v=\rho_v\circ T(a_{v,E})$. The object-membership assertion U_constructible is the direct application of omegaScalar_preserves to the constructible object J(K[1/ell]); this is the finite-valued-closure preservation clause of the compact-support realization dependency, without a new descent claim.

proof.text:
Paste (5) and (6), using naturality of $\rho_g$, and set $z_v=\rho_vT(z_{v,E})$. This gives
$$z_hU(\alpha_Q)=\alpha_\Omega\circ F_g(z_f)\circ z_g(Q_f),\qquad z_v=a_vU(q_v).$$
Apply $U_Z$ to (4) and substitute these identities. Naturality of $a_g$ at $q_f$ gives
$$a_g(P_f)\,U(P_gq_f)=F_g(Uq_f)\,a_g(Q_f).$$
Consequently both paths in the desired square, after precomposition by the invertible $U(q_{g,f})$, equal $z_hU(\alpha_Q)$. Cancel that isomorphism. This proves exactly
$$a_hU(\alpha_R)=\alpha_\Omega\,F_g(a_f)\,a_g(P_f).$$
All displayed maps are natural in $K$, so the equality is natural as asserted.

proof.text: For refinements the system proper/open transformations satisfy horizontal and vertical pasting before evaluation. Compatible towers and common refinements exist for the supplied compactifications, and their formal refinement calculus identifies the chosen-compositor words through these maps. The single-square coefficient theorem includes the noncartesian proper/open squares occurring in a refinement; the ringed refinement coefficient theorem gives their explicit coefficient square. Thus (1), (5), (6) remain commuting squares after inserting every refinement arrow. The compact-support realization theorem gives the corresponding refinement squares for $\beta$, $a$ and their actual total-limit identifications. Naturality of $u,e$ then gives the square for $q$ and for (4). Substituting those squares in Step 8 proves the required compactification compatibility. When $g$ is open choose $(g,1_Z)$. The proper factor is the adjunction-normalized identity, so all its coefficient mates are identities; the remaining word is exact open extension with its stated open unit. Transport by the same refinement squares gives precisely the specified trivial-compactification comparison. This also covers identity arrows, empty schemes and empty opens.
